purpose: Emisar gives AI agents that speak MCP a catalog of declared infrastructure actions instead of a shell. Policy decides what runs, what waits for a person's approval and what is denied, and a small outbound-only runner checks each action again on the host before it runs. This repository holds the Phoenix control plane, the Go runner and MCP bridge, the action-pack catalog and the production infrastructure.

components.what_it_does: Elixir/Phoenix control plane: operator console, website, MCP API, authorization, approvals, audit and billing.
The domain contexts: accounts, runners, packs, policies, approvals and the audit trail.
The web console, the public site and the MCP HTTP endpoints.
Go runner that connects outbound to the control plane and runs declared actions on a host, with its operator CLI.
Go stdio-to-HTTP bridge for local MCP clients.
The versioned catalog of YAML action packs and their behavior fixtures.
Standalone skills customers give their coding agents: install emisar, connect a client, author a pack.
Production Terraform for emisar on Google Cloud.
Go programs behind the ./run contributor command and CI.
Development Compose topologies, images, configs and fixtures.
The root contributor command for development, tests, gates and operations.
Architecture, specifications, runbooks and the rule index.

build_test_run.what_it_does: Prints the setup steps; works before Go is installed.
Starts the sidecars, installs dependencies, migrates and sets up browser tooling in the Coop box.
Loads the explicit, idempotent demo data.
Runs Phoenix with live reload at the URL Coop prints.
Reports every detected tool version and any mismatch.
Runs focused tests for one project.
Runs the Portal gate over what changed.
Runs every project's gate: the local finish line for the whole repository.
Starts the packaged Compose topology with seeded data, three runners, MCP and signing.
Runs the Portal umbrella's tests through its alias.

deploy_release.step: A push to main runs CI and publishes the portal image CI built and tested.
A runner-v* tag releases the runner through the trusted release workflow.
An mcp-v* tag releases the MCP bridge the same way.
Infrastructure changes are applied by hand from infra/, with saved plans.

conventions.rule: Read the root AGENTS.md and the touched project's AGENTS.md in full before editing.
Before 1.0, update every caller and remove superseded code in the same change; no shims, flags or speculative options.
Finish with ./run gate for the project you changed, and report the commands' real results.
Claim implementation work through Coop; done needs green gates, a focused commit with a Coop-Task trailer and coop tasks done.
Deploying, publishing and destructive actions need authority for that action; permission to edit code does not grant it.
Never edit a migration that ran in production; add a new one.

where_to_look.task: Change the console, the site or the MCP endpoints
Change accounts, policies, approvals or audit
Add or change an action pack
Understand the architecture and trust boundaries

open_questions: Who may publish a runner or MCP bridge release, and where the signing keys are held, is not written down here.
